title: Nexus
subtitle: A Brief History of Information Networks from the Stone Age to AI
pitch: The historian behind Sapiens argues that information is about connection more than truth, and that AI is the first technology that can make decisions and create ideas by itself.

chapters.g: Harari's starting claim: information networks connect people, and more information does not automatically mean more truth or wisdom.
How shared stories and written records let huge numbers of strangers cooperate, and the power that gave to those who kept the records.
Why science and democracy survive: they have ways to find and fix their own mistakes, unlike infallible holy books or dictators.
Democracies spread information out, totalitarian states pull it to the centre. New technology changes which works better.

chapters.t: AI as a new kind of member
chapters.g: Computers are no longer just tools that carry messages. They can make decisions and create ideas, so they join the network as agents.
The risk that the world splits into rival digital spheres, and that AI erodes the conversation democracy needs.

ideas: Information connects people; it does not guarantee truth.
Strong institutions need ways to correct their own mistakes.
AI is an agent in our information networks, not just a tool.
AI could strengthen either democracy or totalitarian control.

args.a: AI is unlike earlier information technology because it can decide and create on its own.
args.c: Some historians and technologists think this overstates today's systems, which still depend heavily on human direction.

args.a: We need institutions with strong self-correction to handle AI.
args.c: Critics say this is easy to agree with but hard to turn into concrete policy.

questions: What self-correcting mechanism do you trust most?
Should AI systems be allowed to pretend to be human?
Is more information making your world wiser or just louder?

quiz.q: What is Harari's view of information?
o: It mainly connects people, true or not
It is the same as knowledge
quiz.w: Connection, not truth, is its main role.

quiz.q: Why does he say AI is new?
o: It can make decisions and create ideas itself
quiz.w: It is an agent, not a tool.

quiz.q: What keeps science and democracy healthy, in his view?
quiz.w: They can find and fix their own errors.
